statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The weekend venue closure leaves no live Nasdaq-100 price path to observe, so Tail remains far below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated on hawkish front-end repricing and an unresolved US-Iran tanker exchange around the Strait of Hormuz.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the whole outlook; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: No live Nasdaq-100 price path into a thin 22:00 UTC reopen, with Hormuz flows described as recovering while the US-Iran tanker exchange stays unresolved before a US Labor Day holiday
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,544.16 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, and VIX ended at 14.53 after a contained 13.80-14.58 day range. Friday's internals were rotational rather than directional, with semiconductors broadly higher while several megacaps fell, which argues against an aligned one-way regime being carried into the reopen. The one materially new item verified in the hour since the previous assessment is a US energy-secretary restatement that Hormuz transit is averaging above 9 million barrels a day and that regional flows, including bypass pipelines, have recovered to roughly two-thirds of pre-conflict levels; independent trackers and reporting continue to dispute that arithmetic, though a maritime analytics estimate near 8.6 million barrels a day is broadly consistent with it. That supply-recovery evidence marginally trims the energy component of Stress without resolving it, because the US-Iran tanker exchange around the strait remains active and Iranian officials have warned of a faster and heavier response to further strikes. The other weekend items are unchanged: OPEC+ held October output policy unchanged with the next meeting on October 4, and US diesel set an all-time high near 5.85 dollars a gallon on Friday with distillate stockpiles at historic lows. The rates backdrop is the second Stress channel: August payrolls printed +162k against roughly +53k expected, the 2-year yield reached its highest since January 2025, and H.15 for September 3 shows 2Y at 4.34% and 10Y at 4.77%, with futures pricing a materially higher chance of a hike at the September 15-16 FOMC. Under the tail definition none of this is observed price-path evidence: there is no measurable pullback depth, failed retracement, repeated extension or extreme-hold while the venue is shut, so Tail is held at 5 in the low band and Stress is held at 56 in the elevated band. Conditional risk concentrates in the single 22:00 UTC reopen hour, where the accumulated weekend headline stack would reprice into the thinnest depth of the week; that hour is scored at Tail 21 and maps to WATCH before decaying as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. US cash equities and the Treasury market are closed on September 7 for Labor Day and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout, so no US catalyst falls inside the outlook window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held in a narrow 4-5 band with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress rose from 48 during Saturday's European evening to 57 around the Saturday-night tanker exchange, then oscillated between 52 and 57 across the remaining weekend closure and finished the window at 57. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour, reflecting a closed venue rather than an observed regime.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover seven further closed hours, the scheduled 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday with no US cash open inside the window. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the single reopen hour, which reaches 21 and maps to WATCH where the unresolved Hormuz tanker exchange and the hawkish front-end repricing would meet the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 67 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop before unwinding toward 55. No US macro release falls inside the window, US cash equities and the Treasury market are closed on September 7 for Labor Day and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout; the next scheduled checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI and Oracle earnings on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
